q-68262.worked_solution:

q-100312.name: Question 2
q-100312.worked_solution:
First, we write

$$
3({3}^{5})={3}^{1}\times {3}^{5}.
$$

So our expression can be written as

$$
{3}^{4}\times {3}^{1}\times {3}^{5}.
$$

To multiply powers of the same base, we simply add the exponents:

$$
{3}^{4}\times {3}^{1}\times {3}^{5}={3}^{4+1+5}={3}^{10}
$$

q-100312.html:
Question 2
?

34×3(35)=

a
39
b
320
c
3−1
d
310
e
3−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we write 3(35)=31×35.

So our expression can be written as

34×31×35.

To multiply powers of the same base, we simply add the exponents:

34×31×35=34+1+5=310
q-100312.knowledge_point: Applying the Power Rule for Exponents With Integer Bases

$$

q-185312.name: Question 5
q-185312.problem: Expressed as a fraction in its simplest form, ${9}^{-5}\times {9}^{3}=${{field-1}}.
q-185312.worked_solution:
To multiply powers of the same base, we add the exponents:

$$
{9}^{-5}\times {9}^{3}={9}^{-5+3}={9}^{-2}
$$

To evaluate ${9}^{-2},$ we find the reciprocal of the base $(9)$ and then raise that reciprocal to the same power but with the opposite sign:

$$
{9}^{-2}={(\frac{1}{9})}^{2}=\frac{1}{9}\times \frac{1}{9}=\frac{1}{81}
$$

q-185302.name: Question 6
q-185302.worked_solution:
To multiply powers of the same base, we add the exponents:

$$
{9}^{7}\times {9}^{-7}={9}^{7-7}={9}^{0}
$$

Any number raised to the power of zero is equal to $1.$ So, 

$$
{9}^{0}=1.
$$
